papers.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
papers.abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
papers.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

papers.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

papers.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
papers.abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkan\'e to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}

papers.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
papers.abstract: We prove that the K\"ahlerness of a finitely presented, residually finite group is not determined by its profinite completion, which answers a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober. In the proof, we give explicit constructions to characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions.

papers.title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
papers.abstract:
By a $	extit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $
u$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $
u(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $
u(x)= ot$, where $ ot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{ ot,	op\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of these noetherian forms, and in fact, all noetherian forms of the category of groups.

papers.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
papers.abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.

papers.title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.

papers.title: A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group
papers.abstract: We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.

papers.title: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
papers.abstract: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.

papers.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
papers.abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

papers.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
papers.abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

papers.title: Extreme amenability and failure of the L\'evy property for the trace-class special unitary group
papers.abstract: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a L\'evy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the L\'evy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.

papers.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

papers.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
papers.abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\rho$ affords the character \[ \Omega(\chi)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\chi)/\mathbb{Q})}\chi^{\sigma}, \] for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)$ denotes the Schur index of $\chi$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $\rho$ of $G$ affording the character $\Omega(\chi)$, where $\chi$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.

papers.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
papers.abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: Higher properties T and finiteness properties for twin building lattices
papers.abstract: Properties $[T_k]$ and finiteness properties $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$ and $F_k$ are refinements of the following fundamental notions for groups: Kazhdan property T in the first case, and finite generation/presentation in the last two cases. Under suitable hypotheses on the thickness, we prove that every twin building lattice of $(k+1)$-spherical type $(W,S)$, where $k\geq 1$, has property $[T_k]$ and is of type $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$. If $(W,S)$ is classical, that group is even of type $F_k$. To the best of the author's knowledge, this produces the first examples of infinite finitely presented simple groups with property $[T_k]$ for some $k\geq 2$, and the first examples of finitely presented simple Kazhdan groups that are Frobenius stable and not Frobenius approximable. Along the way, we establish new criteria for property $[T_k]$ for groups acting on CW complexes that extend results of Dymara--Januszkiewicz and Grinbaum-Reizis--Oppenheim. As a key step in our proofs, we determine high acyclicity and, in classical type, high connectivity properties for the opposite complex of a Moufang twin building of $(k+1)$-spherical type and suitable finite thickness.

papers.title: Marginal Congruences and Elements for Two Commutator Words in Completely Regular Semigroups
papers.abstract: Motivated by Problem 13 posed by Ara\'ujo, Ara\'ujo and Kinyon \cite{Araujo2025} concerning marginal elements, subsemigroups and marginal equivalences associated with commutator words in completely regular semigroups, in this paper we investigate the two commutator words $ \omega_1(x,y)=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ and $ \omega_2(x,y)=(yx)^{-1}xy$ on completely regular semigroups. We prove that their marginal equivalences $\sim_{\omega_r}$ ($r=1,2$) coincide and are congruences. More precisely, for a completely regular semigroup $S$, we show that $a\sim_{\omega_r}b$ ($r=1,2$) if and only if $a^0=b^0=p$ and $b^{-1}a\in Z(pSp)$, where $Z(pSp)$ is the center of the monoid $pSp$, and so both words have the same set of marginal elements: \[ M_{\omega}(S) =\bigcup_{p\in E(S)} \bigl(Z(pSp)\cap H_p\bigr), \] where $E(S)$ is the set of idempotents in $S$. We also characterize when this set is a subsemigroup and establish alternative descriptions of the common marginal congruence and marginal elements.

papers.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

papers.title: Finite soluble groups with Sylow subgroups of class at most two are IYB-groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups have nilpotency class at most two is an involutive Yang--Baxter group ($\IYB$-group). This answers a question of Ced\'o and Okni\'nski \cite{CedoOkninski2025}. The main method of the $\IYB$-structures has been reflected in \cite{MengBallesterJimenez2026}.

papers.title: Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.

papers.title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
papers.abstract: The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$. In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $\gamma_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$. Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and nilpotency class $2p-1$ for which the Schur exponent conjecture fails. We show that the Schur exponent conjecture still holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$ generated by at most three elements. For four-generator groups of exponent $p$ and class at most $2p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{M}(G)\cong C_{p^2}^{\,b}\times C_p^{\,a}$ for some $a\ge0$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.

papers.title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.

papers.title: Strong pseudo Frobenius numbers
papers.abstract: By Sylow's theorem, the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, but not every such integer occurs. Frobenius extended the congruence to the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ for every $a\ge0$. Kulakoff and Hall showed that this number is congruent to $1$ or $1+p$ modulo $p^2$ whenever $p^{a+1}$ divides the group order. A positive integer is a Frobenius $p$-number if it is the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ of some finite group for some $a$. There are integers congruent to $1$ modulo $p^2$ which are not Frobenius $p$-numbers, and it remained open whether there are also such integers congruent to $1+p$ modulo $p^2$. We show that no finite group has exactly $106$ subgroups of order $5^a$ for any $a\ge0$.

papers.title: Restrictions to a principal $A_1$-subgroup
papers.abstract: We consider simple simply-connected algebraic groups $G$ over the complex numbers, and a principal $A_1$-subgroup $A \leq G$. We show that for most types of $G$ all its irreducible representations $V(\lambda)$ ($\lambda$ a dominant weight) are determined by their restrictions to $A$ up to graph automorphisms. The exceptions are groups $G$ of type $A_l$ with $l \geq 5$ and $G$ of type $D_l$ with $l = 4^m$ and $m \geq 2$.

papers.title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
papers.abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_{\alpha} C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(\alpha)$ and letting $C_\alpha=\langle\alpha\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_\alpha$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[\alpha]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_\theta H$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.

papers.title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $\Omega$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/\mu_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/\mu_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.

papers.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
papers.abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.

papers.title: Lie algebras graded by the root system $AG_2$
papers.abstract: We study Lie algebras graded by the generalized root system $AG_2$, which is obtained from $G_2$ by adjoining the doubles of its short roots, over fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. We show that every such Lie algebra with a grading subalgebra of type $A_2$ is, modulo its center, the Tits-Kantor-Koecher Lie algebra of a structurable algebra equipped with an idempotent $t$ satisfying $t+\overline{t}=1$. Conversely, every structurable algebra with such an idempotent gives rise to an $(AG_2,A_2)$-graded Lie algebra. We describe the corresponding Peirce decomposition and characterize the additional algebraic structure required for an $(AG_2,G_2)$-grading. Using the classification of central simple structurable algebras, we determine the central simple examples when the characteristic is also different from $5$. Finally, we compare our constructions with the theory of Tits hexagons. For the central simple examples in which all root spaces are non-zero, we determine which ones are Tits-hexagonalizable; in certain cases, this imposes an additional balancing condition on the idempotent.
